text: Look closer at the healthy tissue. Near the base, cells divide by mitosis; their daughter cells move up, become specialised and are eventually lost from the surface. Whether a cell divides again is not left to chance. Genes in the cell control when it goes round the cell cycle, so when cells are lost, division replaces them, and when the tissue is at its size, division is held back. A growing tissue, like a child's, makes more cells than it loses; this adult tissue stays level.
